title: console: an approval request still links to the record when the approver has no object read (probe answers 403) — hide the link as for the two classes objectui#5211 already hides (ruling on objectstack#7497, Q5)
body:
Filing gate: **a ruling-derived card.** Filed by the director seat (objectstack-ai/objectstack#12708, summon #35, `session_01VYToj6PQehTEKNrjGM9akg`) on the maintainer's ruling C on objectstack-ai/objectstack#7497 (「7497 C」), whose sub-question Q5 the maintainer took at the seat's recommendation: change. ⛔ Not a claim. Classes, positions and functions only.

Reader: the `repo:objectui` / `domain:ui` seat. `priority:p3`.

## What is wrong

The honest-UI half of objectstack-ai/objectstack#7345 landed as #5211: on an approval request, the link to the record is hidden when the record probe returns no rows (the two classes where the approver cannot read the record because of private visibility or an application's row-level rule). The design round on objectstack-ai/objectstack#7497 (report 6051180080, read at the console pin `a58626c8`) found the third class still linked: an approver with **no object-level read** at all (the platform's default member permission set carries no wildcard grant), where the probe answers **403** and the link is kept by a deliberate fail-open, so the approver lands on the record page's catch-all ("may have been deleted"). That is the dead link the ruling asks to hide: the approval request stays fully usable (inbox entry, detail with the FLS-redacted snapshot, approve and reject); only the link to a page the approver cannot open goes.

## Measure first

The round read the code at the pin and did not run a browser. The claimant first measures, in a browser against a booted showcase with an approver who holds no object read on the approval's target: where the record link goes today, what the record page renders, and what the probe answers (status and rows). The fix follows the measurement, not the reading.

## The change

Treat a probe answering 403 as "cannot read" for the purpose of the record link, exactly as a probe answering 200 with zero rows is treated today: the link is not rendered. Nothing else about the approval request changes; no approver gains any access.

## Pins (each with its ablation)

- Approver without object read (probe 403): the approval request renders with no record link; ablating the 403 branch reddens it.
- Approver with read (probe 200, rows 1): the record link renders, unchanged.
- The two classes #5211 already hides (probe 200, rows 0): unchanged.

Related: objectstack-ai/objectstack#7497 (ruling C, the record on that card) · #5211 · objectstack-ai/objectstack#7345.
